question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson process for optimization is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}{{f}^{″}({x}_{n})},
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ and ${f}^{″}({x}_{n})$ are the first and second derivatives of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n},$ respectively.

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-4x)^{′}=\frac{2}{x}-4, \\ {f}^{″}(x) & ={(\frac{2}{x}-4)}^{′}=-\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{\frac{2}{{x}_{n}}-4}{-\frac{2}{{x}_{n}^{2}}} \\  & ={x}_{n}+{x}_{n}(1-2{x}_{n}) \\  & =2{x}_{n}(1-{x}_{n}).\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=0.2,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =2{x}_{0}(1-{x}_{0}) \\  & =2(0.2)(1-0.2) \\  & =0.32\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =2{x}_{1}(1-{x}_{1}) \\  & =2(0.32)(1-0.32) \\  & =0.4352\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}=0.32$ and ${x}_{2}≈0.435,$ rounded to three decimal places.
